title: Tenant-aware incident orchestration and status scripting
author: Ava Martinez
summary: Runbook and communications playbook for incidents that affect a subset of tenants (multi-tenant or noisy-neighbor events). This document codifies detection thresholds, triage flows, containment actions, and standardized status/CSR message templates to minimize over-notification while meeting SLAs and regulatory constraints.
audience: SREs, on-call engineers, customer success managers (CSMs), incident commanders, and support leads.
context_and_scope: This guide covers incidents where service degradation is isolated to a subset of tenants or namespaces (examples: noisy neighbor, KV cache eviction storms, per-tenant rate limit misconfiguration, tenant-specific model rollout faults). It does NOT replace global outage runbooks; for platform-wide outages follow the global incident orchestration playbooks.
service_definition: Affected systems: routing-gateway, tenant-router, model-inference-pool, prefix-cache (KV). Primary SLOs referenced: API availability 99.95% monthly, per-tenant 95th request latency < 700ms for hosted API. See SLO matrix page for full definitions.
roles_and_responsibilities:
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates triage and comms.
- Primary Responder: owns initial debugging and mitigation.
- Tenant Liaison (CS): notifies affected customers and crafts tailored comms.
- Platform Owner: coordinates capacity/fallback routing and model rollbacks.
- Security/Privacy Lead: approves any messages containing tenant-specific details.
- Postmortem Owner: authors the post-incident analysis and action plan.
detection_and_alerting_thresholds:
Alerts should be raised when any of the following are observed for a single tenant or tenant-group: 
1) sustained error-rate > 2% for > 5 minutes (where baseline < 0.2%).
2) 99th percentile latency for tenant requests exceeds 2x baseline for > 3 minutes.
3) KV cache miss-rate delta > 30% and eviction rate spike correlated with tenant keyspace.
4) Request routing retries exceed 3x baseline across a tenant's requests.
Each alert must include tenant_id, region, model_id, and function_call_flag where applicable.
initial_triage_checklist:
1) Acknowledge pager and create incident channel (#inc-tenant-<tenant-id>).
2) IC tags incident severity: SEV2 (partial tenant impact) or SEV1 (customer-facing SLA breach).
3) Capture scope: list of affected tenant IDs, regions, models, and time window.
4) Gather quick evidence: top 5 failing endpoints, recent deploys, autoscale events, KV eviction logs, full timeline from observability dashboards.
5) If incident appears tenant-specific, assign Tenant Liaison (CS) immediately.
6) Run tenant-isolation test: replay a tenant request against a clean node pool (if available) to check reproducibility.
tenant_isolation_playbook:
Objective: determine whether degradation is isolated to tenant keyspace or shared infra. Steps:
1) Query routing-gateway logs: filter by tenant_id and compare success rate to platform median.
2) Check model-inference-pool allocation: did tenant land on a degraded GPU host? (node health + GPU memory pressure).
3) Inspect KV cache metrics scoped to tenant prefix: hit/miss ratio, eviction timestamps, TTL churn.
4) If noisy neighbor suspected, trigger targeted rehoming: move tenant traffic to an isolated node pool (command examples below).
5) If rehoming improves metrics within 2 minutes, maintain isolation and prepare customer notification.
Executable commands (examples):
- reroute-tenant --tenant-id t-12345 --target-pool pool-isolated-2
- check-kv-stats --tenant t-12345 --since 10m | grep eviction
Rollback criteria: unsuccessful rehoming or capacity constraints -> escalate to Platform Owner for capacity burst.
containment_and_mitigation_steps:
1) Apply rate-limiter override for the tenant (temporary soft cap) to reduce downstream pressure.
2) Disable background batch jobs that are tenant-scoped and contributing to KV churn.
3) If model variant rollout is implicated, immediately pin tenant to last-known-good model version and scale up the pinned pool.
4) If KV corruption suspected: stop writes to tenant prefix, enable read-only failover to alternate storage.
5) Activate autoscaling burst policy for dedicated pools if commit and policy allow; otherwise coordinate cold migration.
Estimated time-to-stabilize aim: 10–30 minutes for containment, dependent on capacity and rehoming speed.
communication_guidelines: Principles: be timely, accurate, limited to necessary technical detail, and privacy-safe. Targeted customer messages should include: incident summary, impact to tenant, expected ETA for next update, mitigation steps taken, and recommended customer-side workarounds (if any). All targeted messages must be cleared by Security/Privacy Lead when they include tenant-specific logs or indications of data access.
status_page_templates:
Public status page (minimal):
- title: Intermittent degraded performance for a subset of customers
- summary: We are investigating reports of elevated latency affecting some customers in {region}. Impact: increased request latency and intermittent errors for a subset of requests.
- affected services: Hosted API (generation), Tenant Routing Layer
- customer_action: No action required; we will provide updates at least every 30 minutes.
Internal (targeted) status entry:
- title: Tenant {tenant_id} — degraded performance — active mitigation
- details: We observed sustained 99th percentile latency at {value}ms for tenant {tenant_id} starting at {start_time}. Mitigation: traffic rehomed to isolated pool and rate-limiter applied. Next update: {eta}.
Use placeholders exactly as shown. Avoid sharing request/response payloads publicly.
csr_and-enterprise-email_templates:
Subject: Service degradation impacting your Redwood service (tenant {tenant_name})

Hello {contact_name},

We are investigating increased latency affecting a subset of requests for your account ({tenant_id}). Our engineers have isolated traffic and applied mitigations; you may notice a temporary soft cap while we stabilize.

What we know now:
- Start time: {start_time}
- Impact: elevated latency and occasional 5xxs on generation APIs
- Mitigation: traffic moved to isolated node pool; rate limiting applied; model pinned to last known good version

Next steps and ETA:
- We expect an initial stabilization within 30 minutes and will follow up with a full timeline and RCA within 72 hours.

If you have a dedicated contract and require an immediate conference bridge, reply to this message and we will escalate.

Regards,
{liaison_name}, Tenant Liaison (Customer Success)
{incident_link}
in_product_banner_snippet: We are currently mitigating a performance issue affecting some customers in {region}. We expect stabilization within 30 minutes. For status and details see the status page or contact support.
escalation_matrix_table:
| Role | Trigger to escalate | Who to page | Timeline |
| Incident Commander | Unable to contain within 15 minutes or cross-tenant impact detected | Eng Lead on-call, Platform Owner | 15 minutes |
| Tenant Liaison (CS) | Customer requests bridge or SLA threshold breached for paid tier | Head of CS | Immediately on request |
| Security/Privacy Lead | Any indication of data leakage or unauthorized access | Security Pager | Immediately |
| VP Eng | Multi-region customer impact or regulatory exposure | Exec Pager | 30 minutes |
